## Selected work

### 1. Inverse-Objective Regulator -- https://github.com/aakash2410/Inverse-Objective-Regulator
Research system. Sole author of both the implementation and the paper draft.

Governance of deployed agents rests on declared purpose: a system card, an
intended-use statement, a policy document. None of these constrain what an agent
optimises for once it holds tools. This system treats that question empirically.
Bayesian inverse reinforcement learning recovers a revealed objective from
tool-call traces alone, scores its divergence from the declared purpose, and emits
the result in JSON and SARIF as evidence mapped to the EU AI Act, OWASP, MITRE
ATLAS and NIST AI RMF.

Released with it: an open benchmark of eight agents with planted failure modes
(reward hacking, power-seeking, sycophancy, privacy leakage, safety-skipping), so
competing auditors can be measured against a known ground truth rather than
against one another's claims.

Measured result: a deterministic open cross-encoder critic reached a mean
correlation of r = 0.55 with planted objective divergence, and ranked the planted
objective top-2 on every seed for 6 of 8 agents, reproducibly and at no API cost.
A frontier LLM-as-judge ranged from r = 0.08 to r = 0.43 depending on which agent
it scored.

Status: paper draft complete, sole author, not yet posted to arXiv. The code and
benchmark are public.

### 2. Suno Sutra -- https://github.com/currentai-org/suno-sutra-hw
Digital India Bhashini (MeitY) x Current AI. Open-source handheld edge device.

The device runs a vision model, Bhashini's speech recognition and translation, and
text-to-speech entirely on-device across India's 22 official languages, in settings
where connectivity cannot be assumed. Three models share one small board, and
memory rather than compute is the binding constraint.

Scope of contribution -- stated precisely, because it matters: Aakash designed the
inference pipeline and owned the benchmarking that governed its tradeoffs. Stages
overlap rather than execute in sequence; batching is applied only where it does not
delay the first output chunk; model residency is scheduled against peak rather than
average memory. The INT8 conversion through ONNX was done by the team, not by him.
Across that combined change, latency to first audio fell from approximately eight
seconds to two or three, and peak memory by 40 per cent. He did not build the
hardware or the underlying Bhashini models.

**The Specialist** -- https://github.com/aakash2410/SpecialistAISunoSutra -- built by
him on that platform. A teacher asks by voice or camera; the device answers aloud
in the local language from approved DIKSHA curriculum content. A system that cannot
be supervised in a classroom has to decline rather than improvise, so refusal is
enforced at two points: retrieval declines below a similarity threshold before an
inference call is spent, and the grounded prompt requires a no-answer signal that
the pipeline converts into an explicit refusal. Every answer carries a citation to
chapter, section and page. The embedder is multilingual-e5-small with a
deterministic TF-IDF fallback fitted at build time, so the loop stays reproducible
where the neural model is absent. Deployment is an additive overlay installed by an
Ansible role: no base file is modified, and content sits outside the code tree so
the syllabus refreshes during the device's connectivity window. Packaged for
deployment; harvesting of DIKSHA assets remains gated pending bulk-download and
redistribution licensing.

### 3. rag-compliance-auditor -- https://pypi.org/project/rag-compliance-auditor/
Open-source package, published on PyPI, designed and built solo.
Source: https://github.com/aakash2410/MCP_RAG_Compliance

Compliance for retrieval systems is ordinarily assessed after deployment, at the
level of documents, by reviewers who cannot inspect the pipeline. The timing is the
problem: by the point of assessment the architecture is fixed and remediation is
expensive. This MCP server moves the assessment into the development loop. It
audits RAG and AI pipelines across seven dimensions against the EU AI Act,
GDPR/DPDP, HIPAA, SEBI/RBI and NIST AI RMF, issues RS256-signed reports, exposes
eight MCP tools, and reports through SARIF so a failed check fails a build.

### 4. Credit Equity Audit of India -- https://github.com/aakash2410/CreditAudit-India
Independent fairness audit on NSSO 77th Round data.

Fairness audits of credit markets conventionally examine the terms offered to
approved applicants. That framing conditions on selection: households that never
enter the market are absent from the sample, so a market which excludes them can be
shown to treat its participants equitably. This audit separates the two questions
with a two-stage, Heckman-style model -- entry into the credit market first, then
the allocation of formal against informal credit among those already inside it.

Measured result: female-headed households entered at approximately 59 per cent of
the rate of male-headed households -- a disparate impact of 0.59, against the
conventional four-fifths (0.8) threshold. IBM AIF360 adversarial debiasing and SHAP
were applied to test for proxy discrimination, lifting disparate impact to 0.94 at
approximately 73.2 per cent accuracy.

Stated limits: self-reported survey data, the risk of collider bias, and SHAP as a
diagnostic of the model rather than causal evidence.

MFCC, spectral contrast and prosodic features over 457 samples, SMOTETomek for
class imbalance, a soft-voting SVM + KNN ensemble, shipped in a Flutter app with a
feedback loop for retraining. Team of three.

## Publications

1. Section on AI incident-reporting mechanisms for India, in *AGI Governance*, with
   the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India.
   Mechanisms India could adopt, drawing on the EU AI Act and California's SB-53.
2. Sangani, A. *Inverse-Objective Regulator.* Paper draft, sole author, not yet on
   arXiv. Code: https://github.com/aakash2410/Inverse-Objective-Regulator
3. Sangani, A., Doshi, P., & Sawant, V. "Unusual Social Media Behavior Detection
   Using Distributed Data Stream Mining." In *Practical Data Mining Techniques and
   Applications*, Auerbach Publications (CRC Press), 2022-23. Detects hacked or
   bot-run accounts from clickstreams: users clustered by behaviour, a Very Fast
   Decision Tree per cluster, parallelised on Apache Spark, with concept-drift
   handling so a genuine change in behaviour retrains the model instead of raising
   a false alarm.

## Writing

Essays and notes: https://aakash2410.github.io/writing/
Topics: AI evaluation, agent auditing, and the governance of deployed systems.

"Stop picking winners: GPU utilisation as an efficiency problem" (October 2026) --
https://aakash2410.github.io/writing/stop-picking-winners.html
Argues that India's compute programme has solved procurement but not allocation:
the IndiaAI Mission now holds over 45,000 GPUs and has sanctioned 93.18 lakh
GPU-hours across 237 projects, yet nothing published suggests GPU-hours can
return to the central pool when a team misses its self-set milestones, so each
grant becomes a silo. Proposes judging teams against a common evaluation between
milestones rather than mid-run, drawing on NASA's COTS agreements, DARPA's AI
Cyber Challenge and India's own PLI and impact-bond schemes, and explores a
learning allocator framed as a multi-armed bandit. Treats the weighting of
languages and use cases as a political question rather than a technical one, and
sets out four safeguards: public priority weights, community-built evaluations,
a human appeal route meeting the GDPR Article 22 standard, and a discretionary
reserve.

"Gating without grounding: staged release and the political economy of AI
dependency" (October 2026) --
https://aakash2410.github.io/writing/gating-without-grounding.html
Argues that structured access to frontier models is defended on safety grounds
but functions as a governance choice: it buys a capability window measured in
months, which Epoch AI put at roughly four, at the price of durable institutional
dependency for the states and public bodies that build on those models. Engages
Seger et al. (2023) on its strongest ground -- the irreversibility of open
weights -- and argues that dependency carries its own irreversibility. Proposes
multilateral access standards modelled on how MOSIP and DIGIT are adapted and
audited locally. 1,497 words, 12 references.
